question: Let \(A\) be the set \(\{1,2,\ldots,20\}\). Fix two disjoint subsets \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) of \(A\), each with exactly three elements. How many 3-element subsets of \(A\) are there, which have exactly one element common with \(S_1\) and at least one element common with \(S_2\)?

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
